title: Indian Contract Act, 1872 — Section 202 (Termination of agency, where agent has an interest in subject-matter)

content.overview: Where the agent has himself an interest in the property which forms the subject-matter of the agency, the agency cannot, in the absence of an express contract, be terminated to the prejudice of such interest.
content.glance: Agency coupled with interest cannot be terminated to the prejudice of that interest absent express contract.
content.study: Where the agent has himself an interest in the property which forms the subject-matter of the agency, the agency cannot, in the absence of an express contract, be terminated to the prejudice of such interest. This is the statutory form of agency coupled with interest and limits the principal’s general power of revocation under s. 203.

sections.heading: Agent’s interest in subject-matter
sections.body: Agent has an interest in the property forming the subject-matter of the agency.

sections.heading: No termination to prejudice of interest
sections.body: Absent express contract, agency cannot be terminated to the prejudice of that interest.

examples.title: Application of Section 202
examples.body: Facts that satisfy the elements stated in the statutory text of Section 202 produce the consequence described in that section. Do not add elements beyond the text.

hypotheticals.question: Do the facts engage Section 202?
hypotheticals.analysis: Compare the facts with the statutory elements in Section 202. If they match, the statutory consequence follows; otherwise it does not.

questionsAndAnswers.question: How should a Section 202 problem be analysed?
questionsAndAnswers.answer: Identify agent’s interest in the subject-matter; test express contract allowing termination; if none, refuse termination to the prejudice of the interest.

examTips: Agency coupled with interest blocks prejudicial termination.
revisionPoints: No prejudicial termination without express contract
